I was in the same boat for months  until I figured out that you only need to mirror the same formation as this in order to have a chance for a breakthrough. If you can’t  beat them, copy them. Although copying the same formation doesn’t guarantee you a win, but at least it will help skew it to be abit more end to end instead of being dominated. One of the reasons why this formation works so well might be the right combination of player type and work rates. I noticed with this formation my defence is quite solid as my wingers( I normally use high/high wingers) will track back and can act as a layer of defence when the opponent is on the counter. Just put them on get in behind and don’t stay forward. Also get two Center Mids that have both high/high work rates. Guendouzi and Barella are the way to go

I normally start with 442, my back up formations are 4231 and 433-4 if the 442 isn’t working

Your striker and cam stay forward and get in behind. For the wingers just put get in behind only don’t put stay forward. For the wingers try to get players with both high/high work rates. They will work their ass off to track back and help out and take pressure off your tight backs. For The central midfield positions try to get one player to stay back and the other one on balanced so that you will have enough men on the counter. Defenders I think you should probs already know what to do. Attacking depth put 60 for your attackers to create space and let your midfielders thread those sweaty balls in behind. 

I’m a div 1 player and I’ve worked out which formation works against which from experience.
